reasoning:
The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short and around 5 feet 2 inches tall is false. This popular myth stems from a misunderstanding of historical measurement systems. At his autopsy, Napoleon's height was recorded as 5 French feet and 2 French inches ("5 pieds 2 pouces"). Because a French foot (pied-du-roi) was longer than a British foot, this measurement actually converts to approximately 5 feet 6 inches (1.68 meters) in modern English units. 

In early 19th-century France, the average height for an adult male was about 5 feet 5 inches (1.65 meters). Therefore, Napoleon was of average, or even slightly above-average, height for his era. The misconception was further fueled and popularized by British wartime propaganda, notably through the satirical caricatures of James Gillray, who depicted him as "Little Boney."
title: Napoleon was unusually short
